name: Parfum Satori
about: A one-perfumer house run by a French-trained Japanese nose who works almost entirely from Japanese plants, tea, incense culture and seasonal moods.
why: Barely distributed outside Japan, so it is still a discovery for most Western noses. One of the clearest examples of a modern Japanese perfume voice.

sig.name: SATORI (Eau de Parfum)
sig.profile: Imagine the calm of a temple incense ceremony, then add a thread of cocoa and cinnamon. It is built to suggest kyara, the rarest grade of agarwood, without the barnyard heaviness some oud carries: dry, quiet, warm and very straight-lined on skin.

name: SHIRO
about: A Japanese skincare-and-fragrance brand known for soft, clean, everyday scents sold at very gentle prices.
why: Hugely popular inside Japan but little known abroad. The easiest, cheapest way to try the Japanese taste for clean, close-to-skin scent.

sig.name: White Tea Eau de Parfum
sig.profile: Fresh-cut citrus over a cup of green tea, finishing like clean laundry. Light, polite and office-safe; the brand says it lasts about five to six hours.

price.note: Page did not say whether tax is included. Was sold out on the check date.

name: J-Scent
about: A Japanese line that turns everyday Japanese moments (sake, tatami, ramune soda, wet streets) into wearable perfumes.
why: Playful and very place-specific, a good bridge between Japanese culture and Western perfume formats.

sig.name: Hanamizake
sig.profile: Cherry blossom drifting into a cup of chilled sake: a fruity, rice-wine sweetness on top, then soft spring florals and a clean woody musk. Bright and springlike.

price.note: Canadian price from an overseas reseller; it costs much less in Japan.

name: Shoyeido
about: A centuries-old Kyoto incense maker. Not perfume in a bottle, but the root of how Japan thinks about scent (the art of kōdō, 'listening' to incense).
why: Incense is the original Asian perfume. Useful for Clay as a room-and-ritual layer, and a cheap way to learn notes like sandalwood, agarwood and clove.

sig.name: Kyonishiki (Autumn Leaves) incense
sig.profile: Cinnamon and sandalwood smoke meant to recall autumn in Kyoto's Arashiyama hills: warm, spiced and soothing rather than churchy.

price.note: Starting price for the smallest bundle (incense sticks, not ml). Sold out on the check date.

name: Tamburins
about: A Seoul design-led beauty brand from the team behind the eyewear label Gentle Monster. Famous for sculptural stores and egg-shaped perfume bottles.
why: Defines the 'K-scent' look: soft, skin-like, slightly herbal, with art-gallery packaging.

sig.name: Perfume CHAMO
sig.profile: Chamomile tea with a spoon of honey, sharpened by a slightly bitter sage, then settling into pale wood and warm musk. Cozy and calming.

price.note: 11 ml and 14 ml egg sizes also sold.

also.name: Perfume Balm (6.5 g)
also.notes: Solid balm in their scents (Chamo, Pumkini, Berga Sandal, Blue Hinoki...). Apply under spray perfume to make it last longer.

name: Nonfiction
about: A Korean fragrance-and-body brand known for warm, wearable 'skin scents' and a strong cult following across Asia.
why: Shows the Korean move from sweet to grown-up woods and tobacco, at prices well below Western niche.

sig.name: In The Shower
sig.profile: A bitter-orange aperitif poured over smoky tobacco and dry wood. Despite the name it is warm and moody rather than soapy.

price.note: Price reported by a Singapore beauty site; bottle size not given.

name: GRANHAND.
about: A Seoul perfumery with apothecary-style shops, making perfumes, multi-use sprays and scented goods.
why: Very affordable Korean niche with an English store, good for building a first 'Korean shelf'.

sig.name: Marine Orchid (Multi Perfume)
sig.profile: Juicy pear and mandarin over a soft bouquet, finished with a hint of toffee. Sweet but airy; the 'multi perfume' format is meant for skin, fabric and rooms.

price.note: Price shown for the Susie Salmon Multi Perfume 100 ml; the multi perfumes share this format.

name: BORNTOSTANDOUT (BTSO)
about: A bold Seoul house with dramatic, cocktail-like concepts that has started to appear in Western niche shops.
why: The most 'loud' Korean house, a counterpoint to the soft K-scent stereotype.

sig.name: Mad Honey
sig.profile: Rum-soaked honey and rose over thick vanilla and resin. Rich, sticky-sweet and long-lasting; best for cold evenings.

price.note: Bottle size not given in the source.

name: Pesade
about: A small Korean label with an English shop and very low entry prices.
why: One of the cheapest ways to sample Korean indie perfume.

sig.name: Mid Mountain
sig.profile: A clean lemon-and-flowers opening on a soft cedar and musk base. Easy, fresh and versatile.

price.note: Reported price, possibly a sale price; size not given.

name: To Summer (观夏)
about: One of the brands leading China's new 'Eastern' perfume wave, built on tea, osmanthus, magnolia and quiet botanical moods.
why: Chinese niche is the fastest-growing scene in Asia and still almost unknown in Canada. This house is the most approachable entry point and ships internationally.

sig.name: Osmanthus Perfume
sig.profile: Osmanthus is the apricot-and-suede flower that scents Chinese autumns. Here it is juicy and peachy at first, then settles into a soft, clean amber. Also see their Triple Tea, a dry, unsweetened mix of green, black and rock tea.

price.note: 30 ml US$139.90, 100 ml US$279.90 (read from the shop data). Was sold out on the check date.

name: DOCUMENTS (闻献)
about: A Shanghai house started around 2020, known for dark, concentrated perfumes, incense and tea themes, and gallery-like stores. Its themes lean on Chinese materials and Zen calm.
why: Considered the most avant-garde of the new Chinese houses. Mostly sold in China (Taobao/Tmall), so it is truly untapped here.

sig.name: Naive (初熟之物)
sig.profile: The house style: a numbing tingle of Sichuan pepper and bright citrus, then incense smoke, tea and cedar on a resinous, musky base. Meditative and bold at once. (Notes listed are the house's typical palette, not one confirmed formula.)

price.note: No public English price list; check their Taobao or Tmall store.

name: Uttori
about: A Chinese artisan house that reworks familiar Chinese plants, tea and gardens into modern perfumes.
why: Small, story-led and still rare outside China.

sig.name: Moss Rock (苔庭)
sig.profile: Named after a moss garden but softer than it sounds: creamy coconut and pear with tropical white flowers over a soft vanilla wood. Gentle and comforting.

price.note: Price not published in English sources.

name: ICHUN
about: A small Taiwanese perfumer (sold through the YANYANTANG aroma shop) whose scents come from childhood memories of Taiwanese temples and hometown flowers.
why: Taiwan's indie scene is tiny and almost invisible abroad. Temple-inspired perfume is a scent story you won't find in Western lines.

sig.name: Prayer (初一十五)
sig.profile: A visit to a Taiwanese temple on the 1st and 15th of the lunar month, without the heavy smoke: pink pepper stands in for incense sparks, then rose and a warm agarwood-sandalwood base.

name: Bombay Perfumery
about: A modern Mumbai house that tells Indian city and travel stories with Western-style eaux de parfum, many using Indian materials.
why: Modern India in a bottle, at mid prices, with a global store that ships.

sig.name: Chai Musk
sig.profile: A railway-station cup of masala chai: ginger and lemongrass steam, toasted nuts, then a milky, slightly smoky sandalwood. Warm and comforting. Their Seven Islands is the beachy alternative.

name: Gulab Singh Johrimal
about: Delhi's oldest perfumery, run by the same family since 1816. Makes ittars (attars): plant oils distilled the old way into a sandalwood-oil base, plus pure 'ruh' (the first, purest distillate of a flower).
why: Attars are alcohol-free, very concentrated, and almost unknown to Western shoppers. Ruh Gulab (rose) here is among the most respected anywhere.

sig.name: Ruh Gulab (pure rose distillate)
sig.profile: Rose the way the petals smell, not perfume-counter rose: green, honeyed and almost fruity, worn as a drop of oil. Also look for khus (vetiver root), cooling and earthy, and their sandalwood blends.

price.note: Owner's stated range per 10 ml: blended perfumes from about ₹100, pure Ruh Gulab up to ₹28,000. Their own shop sells discovery sets from about ₹1,065 to ₹2,005.

name: Spa Ceylon
about: A Sri Lankan Ayurveda-inspired wellness brand whose perfumes are named after island places: Kandy, Mirissa, Arugam Bay.
why: Sri Lankan scent stories (temple flowers, spice gardens, surf towns) at accessible prices.

sig.name: Kandyan Rose Eau de Perfume
sig.profile: A sugared rose garden: berry-bright rose and jasmine on a candy-soft vanilla base, inspired by the royal flower gardens of old Kandy.

name: Karmakamet
about: A Bangkok scent house in apothecary style, known for perfume oils, solid perfumes and its 'Scentorium', a free walk-through museum of hundreds of smells.
why: Thai scent culture (tea houses, jasmine garlands, Chinese-Thai apothecaries) in oil and balm forms that are rare in the West.

sig.name: Authentic Perfume Body Oil (blends)
sig.profile: Concentrated body oils in blends with names like Tea Chamber, Hainan, Garden Breath and White Space. Oils sit closer to skin than sprays and last well in heat. (Notes per blend are listed on the site.)

name: HMNS
about: One of the brands behind Indonesia's local-perfume boom (pronounced 'humans'), with bold names and earthy, spicy, sweet scents at friendly prices.
why: Indonesia is the source of patchouli, vetiver and clove for the whole perfume world, and its local brands are only now getting noticed.

sig.name: ORGSM Eau de Parfum
sig.profile: Crisp red apple opening onto the three classic flowers (rose, jasmine, peony), then a warm vanilla-amber finish. A sweet, flirty floral and the brand's best known scent.

price.note: Read from the shop's product data (Rupiah).

name: TADHANA
about: A Filipino niche house by ISIPCA-trained perfumer Shale Albao, built on Philippine materials like sampaguita, calamansi, dalandan, almaciga resin and Davao coffee. Prices are in Canadian dollars.
why: A Filipino house with a Toronto link, so shipping and pricing are friendly for Canada. A rare chance to smell Philippine raw materials in fine perfume.

sig.name: Rockstar
sig.profile: Ripe mango and dalandan (a green Philippine orange) with coconut water and creamy island flowers, grounded by vetiver and a touch of agarwood. Sunny but not cheap-smelling.

price.note: 10 ml travel size C$60.

name: Wren Atelier
about: A small Filipino atelier that mixes Manila street food and local flowers with classic perfume materials.
why: Possibly the only perfume with a banana-cue (caramelized street banana) accord. Pure local storytelling.

sig.name: Manila Oud
sig.profile: Calamansi zest and ginger, then sampaguita (the Philippine jasmine) and a caramel-banana note, all sinking into smoky oud, leather and incense. Gourmand meets cathedral.

price.note: Sold through the Yuchengco Museum shop; size not listed.

name: GP Fragrances
about: A Filipino label whose 'Elements' series maps scents to places: Baguio, Banaue, Siargao, Mayon volcano.
why: A scent map of the Philippines; good material for the regional map project too.

sig.name: Baguio Verde
sig.profile: A cool morning in the mountain city of Baguio: pine, mist and crushed leaves over damp soil and vetiver. Green and outdoorsy.

price.note: Sold mainly through Instagram; no public price found.

name: Toouch
about: A new Vietnamese label (2025, perfumer Sy Truong) with one scent per city: Ho Chi Minh City, Da Nang, Hanoi.
why: Vietnam's perfume scene is just forming; this is a city-by-city scent portrait of the country.

sig.name: Smoky Graze (Ho Chi Minh City)
sig.profile: Saigon street coffee and cacao on warm amber. Its siblings: Dreamy Nautica (citrus and sea salt, Da Nang) and Heritage Nuzzle (green tea and soft woods, Hanoi).

name: Maison Bagian
about: Founded in 2018 by Hiệp Nguyễn and Alexandre Perucca: concepts developed in Vietnam, perfumes made in Grasse.
why: A French-Vietnamese bridge, with scents named Hanoian, Saigonaise and Mékong.

sig.name: Hanoian
sig.profile: A portrait of Hanoi; notes to be added after the next check.

name: Amouage
about: Oman's royal-born luxury house, famous for frankincense (Oman's ancient export) and grand, layered compositions.
why: Not untapped, but the benchmark for Gulf-style luxury: frankincense, oud and spice done with Western craftsmanship.

sig.name: Interlude Man
sig.profile: Smoky frankincense and leather with a herbal bite of oregano. Powerful and dramatic; a little goes a long way. (Notes from common listings.)

name: Abdul Samad Al Qurashi
city: Mecca origins; stores across the Gulf
about: A Saudi family house known for oud oils, bakhoor (scented wood chips to burn) and concentrated oil blends.
why: Real Gulf oud culture: oils dabbed on skin and clothes, often layered with a spray. A big step beyond 'oud' as a Western marketing word.

sig.name: Makkah Blend (perfume oil)
sig.profile: A dense, oily oud softened with flowers and musk. Intense and long-lasting; one dab is enough.

price.note: European reseller; sold out on the check date. 0.5 ml sample about US$8.90.

name: Swiss Arabian
about: A long-running Dubai perfume maker selling Arabian-style scents worldwide at low prices.
why: Affordable way to learn the Gulf palette (saffron, oud, rose, praline) before buying luxury.

sig.name: Shaghaf Oud
sig.profile: Saffron and rose over a sweet, nutty praline and soft oud. Warm, sweet and crowd-pleasing; a cold-weather scent.

name: Lattafa
about: The UAE brand behind the Arabian-perfume trend online, famous for rich sweet scents and for close alternatives to expensive designer and niche perfumes.
why: The trend you mentioned. Useful for Clay's 'expensive vs just as good' comparisons.

sig.name: Khamrah
sig.profile: Spiced dates and praline in a warm, boozy-feeling vanilla. Very sweet and very long-lasting; often compared to pricier boozy gourmands. (Notes from common listings.)

price.note: US distributor; size assumed from the standard 100 ml bottle.

also.name: Choco Overdose (Give Me Gourmand)
also.notes: dark chocolate fudge · cocoa powder, cupcake accord · vanilla, caramel, benzoin

name: Nishane
about: An Istanbul niche house drawing on Ottoman stories and Turkish shadow-puppet theatre, mostly in strong extrait concentration.
why: Shows how a non-Western house broke into global niche; the 15 ml size makes it easy to try.

sig.name: Hacivat (Extrait de Parfum)
sig.profile: Bright pineapple and bergamot over mossy, dry woods: a fresh, confident 'chypre' style that many compare to famous pineapple-birch scents.

price.note: Also sold in 50 ml and 100 ml.

name: Saint d'Ici (now Saint VII)
about: Natural, small-batch perfumes by Marie Aoun, made mostly from African materials bought from small farmers and craft distillers, including indigenous plants like buchu.
why: African indigenous botanicals (buchu, ouhout) are almost absent from global perfume. Each natural batch varies slightly year to year.

sig.name: Moussem
sig.profile: Cardamom and rose over aged, earthy vetiver and patchouli. Natural perfumes wear softer and closer to skin than synthetic ones. Also see Nsika, built on the mossy, camphor-like South African ouhout shrub.

price.note: Full bottles are 30 ml with 1 ml samples; current prices at saintvii.co.za.

name: Scentury Perfume & Co.
about: A South African maker of oil-based perfumes, many openly 'inspired by' famous designer scents, plus some original signatures.
why: Local, very affordable, and a clear example of the inspired-by market Clay will compare against originals.

sig.name: Vallée des Roses Oud (Extrait)
sig.profile: A rose-and-oud signature (floral, warm, spicy) in an oil-based extrait. Detailed notes not published.

price.note: Sale price; regular R549.90.

name: Beguile
about: A Nigerian fragrance house making strong, long-lasting perfumes priced for the local market, where big 100 ml bottles and powerful projection are preferred.
why: Nigeria has one of Africa's most passionate perfume cultures, and its own houses are just emerging.

sig.name: Blush Bloom
sig.profile: Almond and vanilla-orchid with creamy tuberose on a soft sandalwood base. Sweet, creamy and feminine. Their Sweet Oud pairs saffron and lavender with smoky oud.

price.note: Prices on their shop; not read on this pass.

name: XINÚ
about: A Mexican niche house built on native Mexican plants: copal, mesquite, vanilla, tobacco, agave and tropical leaves.
why: The clearest 'Mexico in a bottle' line; vanilla itself is native to Mexico.

sig.name: Copala
sig.profile: Copal is the sacred tree resin burned in Mexican ceremonies since Maya times: lemony, smoky, holy. Here it is warmed by mesquite and native vanilla. Powdery-smoky and soothing.

price.note: US retailer Luckyscent; samples available.

name: Coqui Coqui
about: A Yucatán perfumery-and-hotel brand making simple, single-idea scents from local plants.
why: Yucatán orange blossom is sweeter and less bitter than the European kind, a true terroir difference you can smell.

sig.name: Flor de Naranjo
sig.profile: Just orange blossom from Yucatán orange trees: honeyed, fresh and soft. Simple and sunny. Also try their Coco Coco and Tabaco.

name: Fueguia 1833
about: An Argentine house that works like a botanical expedition, using rare South American plants, plant-based musks and long maturing times.
why: Patagonian and Amazonian plants you won't find elsewhere, with clean-formula standards.

sig.name: Agua Magnoliana
sig.profile: A giant Amazonian magnolia tree in bloom: lemony-fresh magnolia petals over soft rosewood and the gentle, incense-like palo santo. Airy and luminous.

price.note: 30 ml $245, 100 ml $408 at the New York store.

name: Natura (Ekos)
about: Brazil's largest beauty brand. Its Ekos line uses Amazon materials (priprioca root, copaiba, pataqueira) sourced with forest communities.
why: Amazon raw materials at drugstore-ish prices, with sourcing stories you can check.

sig.name: Ekos Ryo Chuva
sig.profile: Rain falling on the Amazon: wet citrus, peppery green roots and leaves, then soft florals and a mossy wood base. Fresh and green.

price.note: US store price; size not shown on the page.

name: Zoologist Perfumes
about: A Toronto indie house where each perfume is an animal (Bat, Moth, Beaver, Tiger...), made with different guest perfumers.
why: Close to home, ships from Canada, and one of the most respected indie houses in the world.

sig.name: Deluxe bottles (e.g. Moth, Bat, Beaver)
sig.profile: Each animal is a different scent world, from powdery and soft (Moth) to dark, damp cave and fruit (Bat). Start with their sample sets.

price.note: Most deluxe bottles US$200, a few US$240; size not shown on the list page. Travel sprays and sample sets also sold.

name: Imaginary Authors
about: A US indie house where every scent comes with a made-up book or story.
why: Story-driven and affordable for niche; a contrast to the Asian houses' minimalism.

sig.name: A City on Fire
sig.profile: A struck match, smoke and dark berries over warm resin. Smoky but polished; an evening scent.

name: Goldfield & Banks
about: An Australian house built on native Australian plants and coastlines, with French perfumers.
why: Australian native botanicals (coastal moss, desert lime, sandalwood) are a whole palette most people never smell.

sig.name: Pacific Rock Moss
sig.profile: Sea spray on rocks: salty, herbal and lemony, with a clean cedar finish. Their best seller and a great summer scent.

price.note: Price shown for the default size, assumed 100 ml (50 and 10 ml also sold).

name: Hiram Green
about: A one-man indie house making all-natural perfumes by hand.
why: Proof that fully natural perfume can be rich and long-lasting; a great reference for Safe Batch's 'build from scratch' side.

sig.name: Moon Bloom
sig.profile: A tuberose stem cut fresh: green at first, then a creamy, spicy white-flower heart and a coconut-resin base. Lush and tropical.

name: BOROM
about: A Bangkok luxury house whose scents are named after fabrics and how they feel: cotton, tweed, velvet, cashmere, lace, satin.
why: A fresh Thai concept (perfume as texture) and built to last in tropical heat, which is the main thing its fans praise.

sig.name: LACE VII.XII
sig.profile: The bestseller: a smooth, powdery white floral rather than a fruity one. Creamy lily, jasmine and soft rose with a cool osmanthus-tea thread, resting on a gentle powdered vanilla. Polished and calm, like fine porcelain. Others: Vanilla At First Sight, Japanese Cotton, Sweet Tweed, Red Velvet, Cashmere Unnamed, Naked Satin.

price.note: From your research: Vanilla Collection ฿3,500 and Textile Collection ฿3,900 per 30 ml; Shopee Thailand bundles add free 10 ml travel sizes.

try.label: 10 ml travel size
try.note: Given free with Shopee bundles (your research)

name: Reunrom
about: A Thai scent brand where every perfume, oil and sachet is named after a Thai place: Bangkok districts, floating markets, national parks, provinces.
why: A scent map of Thailand in one shop, with low prices and an English online store. Pairs naturally with your regional map project.

sig.name: Moon Perfume Bangkokian
sig.profile: Bangkok's Pathumwan shopping district as a scent: crisp citrus and apple like the view from a tower, then soft jasmine and rose on clean musk. Easy and bright. Their aromatic oils go further afield, e.g. Doi Pui (roses from a Chiang Mai palace garden) and Sukhothai (lemongrass and herbs).

price.note: Aromatic oils 15 ml ฿890; some 100 ml perfumes ฿1,592.

name: Siam 1928 (Voyager)
about: A Thai house drawing on Thai legends, history and food, with Asian ingredients and ceramic bottles.
why: Possibly the only fine perfume with durian and sticky rice in it. Thai dessert culture as perfume.

sig.name: Golden Hour (Voyager)
sig.profile: Mango-sticky-rice dessert at sunset: green, vanilla-like pandan, a whisper of durian, jasmine and steamed rice over coconut milk and sandalwood. Creamy and surprising.

price.note: Official site lists bottles from about US$100 to US$220.

name: PAÑPURI
about: A Thai spa-and-wellness brand known for natural oils and calm, tea-and-wood scents.
why: Thai spa culture in a bottle, sold in Asian luxury malls.

sig.name: Andaman Sails (Eau de Parfum Extract perfume oil)
sig.profile: Sea breeze over the Andaman coast: bergamot and green tea with a hint of nutmeg on soft sandalwood. Relaxed and spa-clean.

name: Butterfly Thai Perfume
about: A Bangkok niche label with bold incense, oud and spice compositions.
why: Thai take on the oud trend, priced well below Gulf luxury.

sig.name: Incense Oud
sig.profile: Lime and a struck-match gunpowder spark, then temple incense and cinnamon over honeyed oud. Smoky but sweet-edged.

name: MITH Bangkok
about: 'Made in Thailand', also a Thai word for good friendship. Warm, happy scents from botanicals, woods, musk, oud and gourmand notes.
why: Known for a Thai Tea scent; a friendly entry to Thai niche.

sig.name: Nude
sig.profile: Soft pear and peach with peony on a skin-like musk and tonka base. Clean and close. Also look for Thai Tea, inspired by the orange iced milk tea.

name: Solure
about: A Thai drugstore line of scented shimmer body mists, body oils and shower oils named after love moments (First Date, Be Mine, Anniversary).
why: The cheap, fun end of Thai scent; good for Clay's body-mist layering.

sig.name: Body Oil 'Anniversary'
sig.profile: Scented body oil and shimmer mists in sweet, romantic styles. Notes not published.

price.note: Watsons Thailand sale price.

name: POSTES
about: A Seoul brand designed as a little post office: each perfume is a 'letter' from a place, with stamp-style labels.
why: One of the most charming new Korean concepts; now popping up in Tokyo too.

sig.name: From Otaru
sig.profile: A postcard from the snowy canal town of Otaru in Japan: green tea and soft lily on clean musk. Other letters: From Istanbul (black tea, fig, patchouli), From Havana (cherry, osmanthus, leather), From Saint-Tropez (mimosa, sesame, musk).

price.note: ¥9,900 in Japan.

name: YOUSSOFUL
about: A Korean extrait house where each perfume comes with its own illustrated story card and place (Paris, Lourdes, Milan).
why: Extrait strength at mid prices; the brand says scents deepen over the first two months.

sig.name: Je T'aime (Extrait)
sig.profile: A juicy, natural-feeling peony and peach bouquet lifted by mandarin, settling on soft white musk. Romantic and easy.

price.note: US$75 on sale at the time of the check.

name: ROYALWATER
about: A Seoul perfumery with 70+ scents in small bottles, several named after the single aroma molecule they showcase (Iso E Super, Maltol).
why: A fun way to learn what individual perfume molecules smell like, cheaply. Useful background for Safe Batch.

sig.name: Iso E Super (Extrait)
sig.profile: Built on a famous woody molecule that smells like warm cedar and skin, and seems to come and go. Try Maltol 185 for a candyfloss-caramel sweetness.

name: SW19
about: A Seoul brand whose scents are named after times of day and moments (it sells '8am' room sprays, for example).
why: Mood-by-hour perfume, useful for Clay's routine idea of a morning vs evening scent.

sig.name: Time-of-day collection
sig.profile: Scents tied to specific hours (morning, afternoon, night). Notes per scent on their site.

price.note: Full bottles ₩150,000 to ₩165,000 on the official shop; sizes not read.

name: Kinfolk Notes
about: A fragrance line from the makers of Kinfolk magazine: designed in Denmark, made in Korea, with each scent tied to a book, film or place.
why: Scandinavian calm meets Korean craft; their discovery sets make sampling cheap.

sig.name: Captain's Bar
sig.profile: Inspired by a legendary Hong Kong hotel bar: crisp citrus and cypress, a soft violet heart, and a warm vanilla-amber finish. Polished and grown-up. Garden Shower is the fresh floral alternative.

price.note: Eau de parfum 30 ml ₩110,000, 50 ml ₩150,000, 100 ml ₩220,000. Discovery set of 5 ₩25,000.

name: Skybottle
about: A Korean hair-and-body mist brand sold widely online and in Canada (Well.ca).
why: Cheap way to try K-scent styles; easy to buy from Canada.

sig.name: Vanilla Sky (Hair & Body Mist)
sig.profile: Warm, sweet vanilla with coconut and orchid. Light enough for hair.

name: WHIPPED
about: A vegan Korean body-care brand known for hair perfumes in tiny bottles that clip onto a bag as a keyring.
why: Viral format (bag charm perfume); sold in Canadian dollars by a Canadian K-beauty shop.

sig.name: Yujamong Juicy Hair Perfume
sig.profile: Yuja (Korean citron) and grapefruit on clean cotton and musk. Bright and fresh, made for hair.

also.name: Peach Pear Juicy Hair Perfume
also.notes: A vegan keratin hair perfume that smells of ripe peach and juicy pear, sold in a candy-like heart keyring pack; sold through KakaoTalk Gifting in Korea.

name: KST Scent
country: South Korea (Korean-born founder, studio in the US)
about: An indie line by Korean-born Kael Jeong with perfumer James Nguyen, turning Korean childhood treats into perfume (banana milk, hotteok).
why: Korean food memories as fine fragrance; a cult indie find.

sig.name: Banana Milk Coffee
sig.profile: Korea's famous banana milk carton poured into iced coffee: ripe, milky banana, then roasted coffee and a warm, creamy base.

name: COSMIC MANSION
about: A Korean brand of natural-feeling, flower-shop florals for any gender.
why: Clean jasmine florals at mid prices.

sig.name: Another Morning
sig.profile: Walking into a florist first thing: freesia, jasmine and tulip, fresh and dewy.

name: etleé
about: A Korean 'everyday scent' brand with a star theme (the name joins French words for star and studio).
why: A true skin scent at a low price.

sig.name: Skin Scent
sig.profile: Warm, clean skin made a little better: ambroxan, musk and soft woods that melt in.

name: OCT
about: A Kuwaiti fashion label that also sells sweet 'all over sprays' for body and hair, with cake-themed names.
why: Gulf gourmand taste in a light body-spray format, shipping worldwide. Note: their cake ads are labelled as AI-made images.

sig.name: Hot Cakes (All Over Spray)
sig.profile: Strawberry shortcake: whipped cream, strawberry and marshmallow on vanilla. Very sweet and playful. Siblings: Vanilla Crush (marshmallow, caramel, orange blossom) and Creamy Vanilla (vanilla, coconut, white musk).

price.note: Set of 3 sprays 30 KWD.

name: Milky Mane
about: A hair-and-body perfume line in illustrated boxes, with dessert-and-fruit scents and new 20 ml bag-size bottles at Rossmann.
why: Shows the European drugstore side of the gourmand trend. Brand origin still to confirm.

sig.name: 002 Cherry Crush (Hair Perfume)
sig.profile: Juicy cherry and red berries warmed with cinnamon, on a clean musky base. Others: a cinnamon-roll milky scent and a cotton-candy 'Sweeten Me'.

price.note: €26 on offer at the check.

name: Dries Van Noten (Soie Malaquais)
about: The Belgian fashion designer's perfume line, each scent built on an unexpected pairing of two materials.
why: A designer house that behaves like niche; Soie Malaquais is a silky gourmand loved in the Gulf.

sig.name: Soie Malaquais
sig.profile: Smooth as a silk dress: tart blackcurrant and rose, then roasted chestnut, cocoa and vanilla. Cozy, polished and quietly sweet.

name: KITOWA
about: A Tokyo house built on Japanese woods (hinoki, hiba, sugi cedar, kusunoki camphor) and yuzu, best known for alcohol-free, water-based perfumes.
why: Japanese forest bathing in a bottle, and a rare alcohol-free fine fragrance that is gentle on skin. Interesting for Safe Batch too.

sig.name: Eau Éclosion Sandalwood
sig.profile: Creamy sandalwood wrapped in soft, powdery iris, with a lift of lemon and cardamom and a warm musk-vanilla finish. Gentle and cocooning. Their SUGI (Japanese cedar) is the forest-morning version.

price.note: Bottle size not shown on the page; SUGI 50 ml sells for £170 at Japan House London.

try.label: SUGI 50 ml at Japan House London

name: Isak Fragrances
about: An Indian house that sells each scent both as a spray perfume and as an alcohol-free attar oil.
why: Lets you compare the same scent as a modern spray and a traditional attar.

sig.name: A Royal Walk
sig.profile: Green, bitter galbanum and lemon, then cool, powdery orris (iris root) and violet over a polished oud and oakmoss base. Elegant and composed.

price.note: Attar version 12 ml ₹1,190.

name: Naso Profumi
about: An Indian luxury house reworking Indian materials such as khus (vetiver), mitti, rose and tamarind in a modern, quiet style.
why: Indian ingredients made understated rather than heavy.

sig.name: Khus Noir
sig.profile: Khus is the vetiver root Indians weave into summer cooling mats. Here its earthy, smoky-green side is softened into a refined, cool woody scent.

name: NEESH Perfumes
about: An Indian house known for woody orientals and creamy gourmands, including one built on Indian wild vetiver.
why: Captures petrichor, the smell of first monsoon rain, in a modern spray.

sig.name: Haute Vetiver
sig.profile: First rain on hot earth: bright citrus, then the rougher, earthier Indian wild vetiver with a touch of raw cacao and dry woods. Fresh yet grounded.

name: The Perfumatory
about: A Mumbai label with simple, mood-named scents (Rose Oud, Citrus Leather, Bold Vanilla) at entry prices.
why: Very affordable Indian everyday perfume.

sig.name: Bold Vanilla
sig.profile: A loud, sweet vanilla with pear and orange blossom on a patchouli-wood base. Strong trail; good for evenings.

name: SAFF & Co.
about: One of Indonesia's best-known local perfume brands, selling extraits at local prices.
why: Strong extraits at Indonesian prices; part of the local-perfume boom.

sig.name: MECHLINE (Extrait)
sig.profile: A rosy, airy floral: herbal monarda and grapefruit, a soft lotus-rose heart and a powdery violet-musk finish. Light and dreamy.

price.note: Size not shown on the page.

name: Sifr Aromatics
about: A small-batch perfumer on Singapore's Arab Street, making oil perfumes and sprays rooted in Malay and Arab trading history.
why: Singapore's old attar quarter, updated. Sells the same scent as oil or spray.

sig.name: Rajawali
sig.profile: Named for the Malay word for eagle (the Garuda). Bergamot and saffron over glowing amber and sandalwood: warm, regal and smooth.

price.note: 15 ml oil SGD 55; 50 ml eau de parfum SGD 95.

name: Afnan
about: A Dubai house famous online for affordable Arabian scents, including close alternatives to designer bestsellers.
why: Another big name in the Arabian-perfume trend; good for Clay's dupe comparisons.

sig.name: Turathi Electric
sig.profile: A sunny, juicy citrus-and-pear opening over clean amber, musk and a little vanilla. Bright and easy for summer.

name: Universal Flowering
about: A Montreal indie house whose perfumes come with written stories, like letters or film scenes.
why: A local Canadian indie with a strong art voice.

sig.name: Big Night
sig.profile: A glamorous night out: cocktail-cherry and pineapple sweetness cut with bitter herbs and bay leaf over vetiver and musk. Playful and moody.

price.note: 15 ml US$85; sample set available.

name: Monsillage
about: A Montreal perfumery known for playful, natural-feeling scents, including one built around celery.
why: Canadian-made and priced in CAD; one of the most original green scents around.

sig.name: Eau de Céleri
sig.profile: Fresh-snapped celery and cut grass fizz at first, then soften into an elegant green chypre with delicate buds and vetiver. Crisp and surprising.

price.note: 7.5 ml travel spray C$35.

name: Curionoir
about: An Auckland perfumer, Tiffany Witehira, whose Māori heritage shapes her palette and stories.
why: Rare Aotearoa voice in perfume; also makes clay 'relic' solid-perfume pieces.

sig.name: Moon Moss (Extrait)
sig.profile: Moonlight over a wetland: cool hyacinth and lily, a watery algae note, then damp moss, birch and cedar. Calm and mysterious.

price.note: 4 ml pocket parfum NZ$60. Extraits do not ship internationally.

name: The Virtue
about: A small New Zealand studio making perfumes and incense inspired by the Taranaki coast.
why: Wild west-coast New Zealand as scent.

sig.name: Back Beach
sig.profile: A smoky, moody scent with a salty edge, inspired by the wild Taranaki surf beach. Also sold as hand-dipped incense.

name: Diptyque
about: A Paris house started in 1961 by three artists as a fabric-and-curiosities shop on boulevard Saint-Germain. Famous for its oval labels, candles, and natural-feeling, travel-inspired scents (several drawn from a founder's childhood in Vietnam).
why: Your favourite, and the reference point for the 'quiet, artistic, nature-first' style. Houses tagged 'If you love Diptyque' share that feel.

sig.name: Philosykos (Eau de Parfum)
sig.profile: A whole fig tree on a hot Greek afternoon: green, milky fig leaves, a little sweet fruit, then dry pale wood from the trunk and bark. Fresh and creamy at once; the eau de parfum leans more woody than the original toilette.

price.note: Price from the European shop; the Canadian site prices in CAD. Holiday editions sell at the same price.

also.name: Tam Dao (EDP)
also.notes: Creamy sandalwood with cypress, cedar and a breath of Asian spice, inspired by a Vietnamese temple forest.

also.name: Do Son (EDP)
also.notes: Tuberose and orange blossom carried on a sea breeze, from a childhood beach in Vietnam. Rich but airy.

also.name: Orphéon (EDP)
also.notes: A smoky 1960s Paris jazz bar: juniper, a little jasmine, tonka and cedar. Soft and woody.

also.name: Fleur de Peau (EDP)
also.notes: Powdery iris and pink pepper over warm, skin-like musk and ambrette. Intimate and clean.

also.name: Eau Rose (EDP)
also.notes: A bright, fresh-cut rose with a lychee-like juiciness. Easy everyday rose.

name: BYREDO
about: A Stockholm house known for minimal bottles and memory-based scents, each told in a few words.
why: Same calm, artful feel as Diptyque with a Scandinavian, more minimal twist. Has a Canadian online store.

sig.name: Gypsy Water
sig.profile: A campfire in a pine forest: bright citrus and juniper, then incense smoke and pine needles, settling into soft vanilla sandalwood. Woody, cozy and genderless.

price.note: Canadian store price; size taken from the product link.

name: Officine Universelle Buly 1803
about: A revived 19th-century Paris apothecary selling water-based perfumes, oils, powders and combs in beautiful old-fashioned shops (including in Japan).
why: Diptyque-like Parisian heritage charm; its water-based 'Eau Triple' perfumes are alcohol-free.

sig.name: Eau Triple Oud de Médine
sig.profile: A gentle, water-based oud that sits softly on skin rather than shouting. Their perfumes are designed to be noticed only up close.

price.note: Size not shown on the page.

name: Goutal Paris
about: Annick Goutal's Paris house, founded on light, natural-feeling citrus and floral scents, many tied to personal memories.
why: A classic French 'garden' style that Diptyque fans often love.

sig.name: Eau d'Hadrien
sig.profile: Tuscan summer in a glass: sharp lemon and grapefruit softened by green cypress. Clean and timeless. For something sweeter, Petite Chérie is pear, rose and vanilla.

price.note: Petite Chérie 30 ml €95.

name: Essential Parfums
about: A Paris house that gives famous perfumers a single key ingredient and sells the results at fair prices in refillable bottles.
why: Big-name perfumers at accessible prices, with refills.

sig.name: Bois Impérial (Extrait)
sig.profile: A modern woody scent with a fresh herbal lift; the extrait version is darker, richer and twice as concentrated.

name: Matière Première
about: A Grasse-rooted house where each perfume showcases one raw material, often from its own organic fields.
why: Ingredient-first perfumery, useful background for Safe Batch.

sig.name: Metal Lavender
sig.profile: Lavender as you would smell it in a steel distillery in Provence: clean, cool and slightly metallic rather than soapy.

name: Ormaie
about: A mother-and-son Paris house using mostly natural materials in refillable bottles with wooden caps.
why: Natural-leaning, literary scents in the same spirit as Diptyque.

sig.name: Papier Carbone
sig.profile: The smell of old novels on wooden shelves, with a soft liquorice sweetness. Quiet and nostalgic.

price.note: US shop price; 20 ml US$159, refills sold.

name: État Libre d'Orange
about: A cheeky Paris house known for provocative names and surprisingly wearable scents.
why: The playful opposite of Diptyque's calm, at fair niche prices.

sig.name: You or Someone Like You
sig.profile: A cool, minty, green rose on a hot Los Angeles day. Bright, airy and very easy to wear.

name: Serge Lutens
about: The Paris artist's house, famous for rich, dark, resinous compositions.
why: A historic niche house; the opposite end from light colognes.

sig.name: Fille en Aiguilles
sig.profile: Sun-warmed pine needles and sticky resin on a Mediterranean beach, with a little candied fruit. Warm and resinous.

name: Memo Paris
about: A Paris house of travel-diary perfumes, each named after a place (Marfa, Inlé, Irish Leather).
why: Travel scents like Diptyque's, but bolder.

sig.name: Sky Paris Sky
sig.profile: A tribute to the Art Deco dome of Galeries Lafayette: creamy cocoa butter and vanilla over soft woods and amber.

price.note: Galeries Lafayette exclusive.

name: Maison Crivelli
about: A Paris house built on 'unexpected encounters' between materials, with strong, long-lasting extraits.
why: Big, vivid scents loved in the Gulf.

sig.name: Hibiscus Mahajád
sig.profile: Hibiscus tea in a gemstone market: tart, ruby-red hibiscus and rose against soft vanilla, leather and musk. Very long-lasting.

name: Floral Street
about: A London brand of bright, fun florals in recyclable pulp packaging.
why: Affordable, playful UK floral perfumes.

sig.name: Electric Rhubarb
sig.profile: Chilled prosecco in a summer garden: tart rhubarb and salty air with creamy gardenia on soft sandalwood.

price.note: 50 ml plus 10 ml bundle.

name: Ormonde Jayne
about: A London house known for rare materials and refined, warm compositions.
why: Elegant British niche; strong on saffron and oud.

sig.name: Bijou Zafran
sig.profile: A smouldering saffron scent that stays close and warm rather than loud.

price.note: 2 × 10 ml travel set €90.

name: Miller Harris
about: A London house making natural-feeling, English-garden and tea scents.
why: Gentle and botanical like Diptyque.

sig.name: Citron Citron
sig.profile: Mediterranean citrus groves: sunny mixed citrus over dry herbs and crisp wood. Their Tea Tonique adds bergamot, Earl Grey, maté and birch.

name: Penhaligon's
about: A London perfumer dating back to the Victorian era, known for its bow-tied bottles and animal-head 'Portraits'.
why: British heritage perfumery.

sig.name: Luna
sig.profile: A moonlit garden: bright orange and soft jasmine-rose that fade into a gentle woody fir finish.

name: Officina Profumo-Farmaceutica di Santa Maria Novella
about: One of the world's oldest pharmacies, started by Dominican monks in Florence. Still makes colognes from centuries-old recipes.
why: Perfume history you can still buy; light, classic colognes.

sig.name: Acqua della Regina
sig.profile: The cologne said to have been made for Catherine de' Medici in 1533: bright citrus, orange blossom and herbs on soft musk. Clean and timeless. Melograno adds pomegranate and rose.

name: Xerjoff
about: A Turin luxury house known for rich, high-concentration perfumes and jewel-like bottles.
why: Italian luxury niche; very popular in the Gulf.

sig.name: Torino25
sig.profile: A celebratory, elegant scent tied to the brand's tennis partnership. Notes per scent on their site.

name: Nasomatto
about: Alessandro Gualtieri's Amsterdam-based project of cryptic, very strong extraits in wooden-cap bottles.
why: Cult niche; tiny 30 ml bottles of very concentrated scent.

sig.name: Baraonda
sig.profile: A boozy, woody, raw-skin scent; the brand describes ideas rather than notes. Powerful, so one spray is enough.

price.note: 4 ml perfume oil €55.

name: Vilhelm Parfumerie
about: A Paris house by a Swedish founder, with colourful bottles and story-led scents.
why: Modern Paris niche with Scandinavian polish.

sig.name: Dear Polly
sig.profile: A cup of black tea at dawn: bergamot and apple, warm Ceylon tea and a soft mossy musk. Cozy and polished.

name: Mizensir
about: The Geneva house of master perfumer Alberto Morillas, known for clean, luminous woods.
why: A famous perfumer's own brand; precise and clean.

sig.name: Bright Wood
sig.profile: Dawn light through a quiet room: warm, glowing woods and soft musk. Clean and calm.

name: BDK Parfums
about: A Paris house of modern, sensual scents named after Parisian life.
why: Gris Charnel is a cult fig-tea-iris scent.

sig.name: Gris Charnel
sig.profile: A soft grey cashmere scarf: fig and black tea with powdery iris on a creamy sandalwood base. (Notes from common listings.)

name: Claus Porto
about: Portugal's oldest soap and fragrance house (1887), famous for Art Deco-patterned wrapped soaps.
why: Portuguese heritage scent; lovely gifts.

sig.name: Le Parfum
sig.profile: Their perfumes echo the classic soap scents: citrus, florals and fresh herbs.

price.note: Size not shown on the list page.

name: KORRES
about: A Greek pharmacy-born natural beauty brand with sunny Aegean scents.
why: Mediterranean beach scents at drugstore prices.

sig.name: Aegean Bronze (Eau de Parfum)
sig.profile: Warm skin after a day on a Greek beach: citrus, frangipani and caramelised sugar on a sandy vanilla musk.

name: Skandinavisk
about: A Danish B Corp brand that bottles Nordic landscapes, made in France.
why: Nordic forest calm; scents built heavily on essential oils.

sig.name: Deep Førest
sig.profile: A walk through a Nordic boreal forest: cool eucalyptus, pine and cypress over earthy vetiver and cedar.

name: Janua
about: A Thai drugstore perfume brand built on 'new beginnings': young, sweet, fluffy and fruity scents in colourful bottles, including a collaboration with singer BamBam.
why: The budget opposite of BOROM; a full 30 ml bottle costs less than a coffee in Canada.

sig.name: Bonnie Bo
sig.profile: A bright, juicy fruit salad (peach, mango, pear, citrus and tart rhubarb) over soft white flowers, drying down to a clean, powdery vanilla musk. Playful and fresh, and it smells more expensive than it is. Others: Dreamy Cloud, Sweetie Picnic, Kiss Me More, and the BamBam line.

price.note: Watsons Thailand ฿199 to ฿339 per 30 ml (member prices about 10% lower). International resellers about US$13 to US$20.

alt: Marc Jacobs Daisy Ever So Fresh

name: LOE (Life on Earth)
about: A Korean clean-beauty brand making simple 'everyday comfort' scents (fresh laundry, flower shops, cut grass) plus solid perfume sticks and diffusers.
why: Clean, cozy skin scents; ships from a US store.

sig.name: White Shirts
sig.profile: The warmth between a crisp white shirt and your skin: watery flowers, clean soap and soft musk. Also: Harsh Green, Laundry Scent, Sincere Wood.

price.note: About US$30 at Shilla Duty Free (from your research).

alt: Maison Margiela Replica Lazy Sunday Morning

name: Wick Fragrances
about: A Cape Town house that started with candles and now hand-pours perfumes and solid perfumes, with gourmand and volcanic-earth themes.
why: Artisanal South African scent at mid prices; each bottle comes with a 2 ml tester.

sig.name: Sugar & Hyde
sig.profile: Fig, cardamom and black tea, then a dark, boozy turn of bourbon and leather softened by tonka. Chic with an edge.

price.note: May not be the same brand as the 'WICK PARFUMS' case in your Thai screenshot. Wicked Fragrance House in Canada looks like a separate home-decor shop.

alt: Maison Margiela Replica By the Fireplace

try.label: 2 ml tester included with every bottle

name: L'Artisan Parfumeur
about: One of the first niche houses (1976), known for airy, natural-feeling scents of fig, green leaves and faraway places.
why: A close cousin of Diptyque in spirit; Timbuktu is a cult incense scent.

sig.name: Timbuktu
sig.profile: Dry, airy incense from a West African market: a lift of cardamom and green mango, then papyrus and smoky vetiver. Light but haunting. (Notes from common listings.)

price.note: From your research: standard eaux de toilette €170 per 100 ml; premium eaux de parfum €250.

name: Editions de Parfums Frédéric Malle
about: A Paris 'publisher' that gives star perfumers free rein and credits them by name on the bottle.
why: Some of the most respected perfumes in the world; prices vary by how costly the ingredients are.

sig.name: Carnal Flower
sig.profile: A huge, lifelike tuberose with a cool green-eucalyptus start and a creamy coconut-musk finish. Lush and grand. (Notes from common listings.)

price.note: From your research: about C$410 to C$440 per 100 ml for scents like Lipstick Rose; C$530 to C$570 for richer ones like Carnal Flower.

name: Acqua di Parma
about: An Italian house founded on a 1916 citrus cologne, now with sunny Mediterranean lines.
why: Classic Italian freshness; Blu Mediterraneo is the easy summer range.

sig.name: Colonia
sig.profile: Sicilian citrus and herbs over soft woods: the clean, sharp-dressed barbershop cologne of old Italy. (Notes from common listings.)

price.note: From your research: Blu Mediterraneo eaux de toilette about C$230 to C$250 per 100 ml; Signatures of the Sun eaux de parfum about C$378.

name: Frau Tonis Parfum
about: A Berlin perfumery near Hackescher Markt making vegan perfumes, many tied to Berlin itself.
why: Its Linde Berlin captures the linden trees that line Berlin's streets.

sig.name: No. 10 Linde Berlin
sig.profile: A Berlin summer evening under the linden trees: soft, honeyed, slightly green blossom. Gentle and nostalgic.

price.note: From your research: eaux de parfum €85 per 50 ml; Parfum Intense €120; 100 ml from €115 to €160.

name: Ramón Monegal
about: A Barcelona perfumer from a family fragrance dynasty, known for inkwell-style bottles and a 'Spanish Style' line.
why: Spanish niche with flamenco-inspired scents.

sig.name: Olé
sig.profile: Part of the Spanish Style line (with Flamenco and Bravo), inspired by Spanish passion and colour. Notes per scent on their site.

price.note: From your research: Spanish Style line €195 per 50 ml; Essential and Ibiza collections €135 to €180; 100 ml up to €275.

name: Agonist
about: A Swedish house known for Nordic minimalism and rare hand-blown Kosta Boda glass editions.
why: Scandinavian art-glass perfume; the standard glass line is the accessible one.

sig.name: Standard eau de parfum line
sig.profile: Concept-led scents inspired by Swedish nature and culture. Notes per scent on their site.

price.note: From your research: standard eaux de parfum about €140 to €165 per 50 ml depending on the seller.

name: Perfumehead
about: A Los Angeles luxury house with two strengths: 'Coltraits' (cologne-strength extraits) and full extraits.
why: Very high-end indie with names like Cosmic Cowboy and Canadian Tuxedo.

sig.name: Reine des Anges
sig.profile: A queenly rose: Turkish rose warmed with saffron, with a green, earthy angelica root and vetiver base.

price.note: Coltraits US$235 per 50 ml; extraits US$395 per 50 ml (read from their shop; LA origin from your research).

name: Histoires de Parfums
about: A Paris house whose perfumes are named after a year and the historical figure born in it (1828 is Jules Verne).
why: Seen on the Musinsa Beauty shelf in your screenshot; literary and well priced for niche.

sig.name: 1828 (Jules Verne)
sig.profile: An explorer's scent: bright citrus and eucalyptus, peppery spice and a woody, piney base. Fresh and adventurous. (Notes as printed on the bottle in your screenshot.)

price.note: Price not yet checked.

name: Michael Malul
country: North America (shop in USD and CAD)
city: Origin not stated on the brand site
about: A fragrance brand started by a founder who came from luxury perfume retail, aiming for 'scents people actually want to wear'. Known for story-led ranges like Citizen Jack, Jet Black and the paired 'Latte+Nectar' style duos, at mid prices.
why: Your pick. Good value for 100 ml bottles, 10 ml minis for C$-friendly trying, and a Canadian shop setting.

sig.name: Latte+Nectar
sig.profile: A caramel iced coffee in a sunny café: juicy clementine and nectarine with dulce de leche, a soft orange-blossom and coffee heart, and a creamy whipped-cream amber finish. Also: Citizen Jack (melon, sage, vetiver, tonka) and New Journalist (citrus, lavender, vetiver).

price.note: Most scents US$130 to US$140 per 100 ml; the shop can switch to Canadian dollars.

name: KAYALI
about: A Dubai brand by Mona Kattan, built on Middle Eastern layering culture: each perfume is numbered and designed to be stacked with others.
why: Gulf layering made playful; huge with gourmand fans.

sig.name: Yum Vanilla Cupcake | 108
sig.profile: A birthday cupcake: sugary lemon and sprinkles, then caramel, toasted coconut and warm milk on a thick vanilla-frosting base. Pure fun.

price.note: 100 ml AED 559.

name: Sana Jardin
city: London, with flower harvesters in Morocco
about: A brand that works with women flower harvesters in Morocco, turning leftover flowers into income for them. Vegan, essential-oil-led scents.
why: Social-impact perfume with North African roots; low entry prices on some scents.

sig.name: Nubian Musk
sig.profile: A warm skin musk wrapped in rose and jasmine, with smoky vetiver and creamy sandalwood underneath. Sensual and close.

price.note: 100 ml £90; other scents £115 per 50 ml.

name: Floraïku
about: A Paris house inspired by Japanese haiku, tea ceremony and bento-box presentation; each perfume reads like a short poem.
why: Japanese aesthetic from a French house; tea notes galore.

sig.name: One Umbrella For Two
sig.profile: Sharing an umbrella in the rain: juicy blackcurrant meets nutty, toasted-rice genmaicha tea on soft cedar. Sweet and cozy.

price.note: 10 ml €60; 30 ml €180; 50 ml with 10 ml refill €295.

name: D.S. & Durga
about: A New York husband-and-wife house known for wildly specific, story-rich scents (from pistachio to corpse flower).
why: Playful American indie; Pistachio is a cult gourmand.

sig.name: Pistachio
sig.profile: Freshly cracked pistachios with cardamom and raw sugar, deepening into toasted almond and finishing on creamy vanilla musk. Nutty rather than dessert-sweet.

name: Arquiste
city: New York, founded by Mexican architect Carlos Huber
about: A house that recreates exact historical moments in scent, each with a date and place, founded by a Mexican-born architect.
why: History as perfume; strong Mexican and Spanish storytelling.

sig.name: Almond Suede
sig.profile: Medieval Córdoba's almond sweets: marzipan, honey and orange blossom softened by smooth suede and a smoky hint of pine tar. Addictive gourmand.

name: Henry Rose
about: Michelle Pfeiffer's brand, known for full ingredient transparency and safety-screened formulas.
why: Ingredient transparency fits your Safe Batch and Clay values.

sig.name: Flora Carnivora
sig.profile: A white floral 'with bite': powerful yet soft, creamy yet a little carnal, made to be genderless.

name: Maya Njie
about: A Stockholm perfumer of Swedish and Gambian heritage who makes small-batch scents from memories and nature.
why: Tiny Scandinavian studio, affordable for niche.

sig.name: Vanilj
sig.profile: A cozy vanilla with a slightly boozy, bourbon-like edge. Warm and simple.

price.note: Shop shown in GBP from abroad.

name: 27 87 Perfumes
about: A Barcelona studio making playful, unexpected scents, including yearly archive editions (durian, gin, lavender).
why: Mediterranean indie with a sense of humour.

sig.name: Hakuna Matata
sig.profile: Carefree and tropical: ripe banana and honey with bright bergamot and a heady southern-Chinese jasmine.

name: Rogue Perfumery
about: A one-man US indie reviving old-school, oakmoss-rich classic perfumery.
why: Vintage-style perfume at indie prices; full sample set for US$45.

sig.name: Jasmin Antique
sig.profile: A warm summer night full of jasmine, spiced with clove and softened by musk and vanilla. Classic and heady.

price.note: 75 ml US$156; full sample set US$45.

name: Sultan Pasha Attars
about: A cult British artisan making very concentrated attar-style perfume oils with rare natural materials, in tiny batches.
why: For serious oil lovers; sold by the millilitre, with a free sample of the same blend.

sig.name: Shirin Chai
sig.profile: Persian spiced rose tea: rose, saffron and cardamom over honeyed jasmine, drying down to black tea, beeswax and tobacco. Rich and luxurious.

name: Libertine
about: A Vancouver house making bold, artful perfumes and incense cones, priced in CAD.
why: Canadian-made and Canadian-priced, with travel sizes.

sig.name: Fruit Thieves
sig.profile: Stolen fruit over a fence: sticky, sour passionfruit and green vines, juicy and a little wild.

price.note: 100 ml C$290 (website exclusive).

name: Liquides Imaginaires
about: A Paris house built on myths and legends, plus an 'upcycled' citrus line.
why: Fairy-tale perfume with real craft.

sig.name: Blanche Bête
sig.profile: Inspired by the unicorn: pale, luminous white flowers with a soft, milky glow.

name: Ellis Brooklyn
about: A clean-beauty New York brand of easy, cozy scents in eau de parfum, hair and body mist formats.
why: Gourmand rice scents that echo the Asian 'rice milk' trend.

sig.name: Vanilla Rice
sig.profile: Warm toasted rice and coconut milk with vanilla, lifted by sweet cherry blossom and jasmine. Soft and comforting.

price.note: Size not shown on the page.

name: Parfums Dusita
city: Paris, by Thai perfumer Pissara Umavijani
about: Classic French perfumery made by a Thai-born perfumer, inspired by her poet father and Thai culture (Erawan, La Douceur de Siam).
why: The bridge between Thai heritage and Paris craft; rich, natural-feeling florals.

sig.name: La Douceur de Siam (house style)
sig.profile: Rich, nectar-heavy white florals in the spirit of Thai flower garlands: real jasmine, creamy frangipani and honeyed blossoms, made with old-school French technique. Look also for Erawan and the extraits Le Sillage Blanc and Oudh Infini.

price.note: From your research: eaux de parfum €150 per 50 ml; extraits €195 to €220.

name: Zielinski & Rozen
about: An old-world apothecary-style house from Jaffa with medicine-bottle packaging; each perfume is named simply after its key notes.
why: Bohemian, spice-market scents at one flat price.

sig.name: Black Pepper & Vetiver
sig.profile: Sharp black pepper and bright neroli over dry vetiver and warm amber: like walking through an old spice market. Minimal and grounded. Rosemary & Lemon is the fresh alternative.

price.note: Every 50 ml perfume is €95 (read from their shop).

name: Areej Le Doré
about: A tiny artisan house making natural oud and resin extraits in limited batches that sell out quickly.
why: For serious oud lovers; past batches resell for much more.

sig.name: Limited batch extraits (house style)
sig.profile: Raw, thick and resinous: ancient forest, burning incense and dark damp earth. Very long-lasting and complex.

price.note: From your research: about US$220 to US$350 per batch release (30 to 50 ml).

name: Bortnikoff
about: Natural perfumer Dmitry Bortnikov pairs wild agarwood with classic French florals and gourmand notes.
why: The softest way into real oud: wood made wearable with chocolate, coffee and honey.

sig.name: Extraits (house style)
sig.profile: Dark, wild agarwood smoothed with cocoa, coffee and honey, so the wood feels warm and edible rather than harsh.

price.note: From your research: extraits about US$240 to US$320 per 50 ml.

name: Ensar Oud
about: A specialist distiller of wild-harvested oud oils from Asia, plus pure oud spray perfumes.
why: The top end of real oud; oils from hundreds to thousands of dollars.

sig.name: Oud oils and sprays (house style)
sig.profile: Uncompromising, raw oud: deep forest, resin and smoke, with every batch smelling a little different.

price.note: From your research: spray perfumes from about US$350 to US$550 (30 to 50 ml); oils cost much more.

name: Pekji
about: An Istanbul indie making surreal, conceptual extraits (Flesh, Purpl, Blacklight).
why: Avant-garde and artistic; very different from classic Turkish scents.

sig.name: Extraits (house style)
sig.profile: Industrial woods rather than a forest: dry smoky cedar, warm asphalt and burnt resin. Sharp and modern.

price.note: From your research: extraits US$165 per 50 ml.

name: Aftelier Perfumes
about: Mandy Aftel's 100% natural botanical perfumery, using no synthetics at all.
why: A reference for all-natural perfume; useful inspiration for Safe Batch.

sig.name: Botanical perfumes (house style)
sig.profile: Close to the skin and alive: bright citrus, real rose and warm, jammy tree resins that change with your body chemistry.

price.note: From your research: eaux de parfum US$210 per 30 ml; 7 ml pure liquid perfume US$240.

name: Strangers Parfumerie
about: A Thai 'creative laboratory' by Prin Lomros with cinematic, pop-culture scents that range from playful to experimental.
why: An accessible Thai indie with bold ideas.

sig.name: Experimental line (house style)
sig.profile: Anything goes: fizzy soda and fruit at one end, hot irons, tobacco and salty skin at the other. Fun to explore.

price.note: From your research: about US$90 per 30 ml.

name: Phlur
about: A viral modern brand of 'second skin' scents such as Missing Person, Father Figure and Heavy Cream; sold at Sephora Canada.
why: Easy to buy in Canada at one flat price.

sig.name: Missing Person
sig.profile: Like warm, freshly washed skin: soft white musk and a sheer jasmine over light creamy woods.

price.note: From your research: every 50 ml eau de parfum C$134.

also.name: Heavy Cream
also.notes: A milky, creamy skin scent.

name: Bath & Body Works
about: The mall staple for body mists, lotions and candles, with themed seasonal and Disney Princess collections.
why: The budget side of the 'smells like' trend: creators pair its 236 ml mists with luxury perfumes they resemble. Easy to buy in Canada.

sig.name: Disney Princess Belle (Fine Fragrance Mist)
sig.profile: A soft rose and sunny-flower mist on a creamy, whipped base (notes as pictured in your screenshot). Often compared to Parfums de Marly Delina. See the budget twins list for its other luxury look-alikes.

price.note: Canadian regular price reported in 2022; check current price and frequent sales.

name: CYKLAR
about: A US brand of layerable perfume oils in small square bottles, plus a silicone bag charm that slips over the cap so the scent hangs from your bag.
why: A clear example of packaging as an accessory: the perfume becomes part of the outfit. Good inspiration for Clay and Safe Batch packaging.

sig.name: Sex Musk (Perfume Oil)
sig.profile: An intimate, enveloping skin musk that stays close. Others to layer: Vanilla Verve (spicy creamy vanilla), Naked Neroli, Bergamot Bond, Amber Hour, Rose Bud, Core Vetiver, Sacred Santal.

price.note: Silicone bag charm US$15; 4-oil layering set US$115.

name: Cloon Keen
city: Galway (21a High Street), with a shop in Powerscourt Townhouse, Dublin
about: A Galway perfume and candle house started over twenty years ago by Margaret Mangan. Scents are composed and hand-poured in the west of Ireland and draw on Irish myth, music, wool and weather; bottles are refillable.
why: The most complete Irish niche house, and you can smell the whole line in Dublin city centre. Its incense-and-rose side suits cold, damp days.

sig.name: Róisín Dubh (Eau de Parfum)
sig.profile: A dark, bookish rose: damask petals pressed between old pages and inky patchouli, drying down to smoky church incense, pepper and tobacco. Named after a 16th-century song that Irish writers took up as a symbol of the country.

price.note: Refill bottle: €235 for 200 ml.

try.label: 10 ml travel set of three (Lá Bealtaine, Bel Étage, Báinín)

also.name: Báinín (EDP)
also.notes: Named after the creamy wool of Aran jumpers: soft violet, tonka and airy musk with gorse, wet herbs and the smell of rain on warm ground.

also.name: Frosted Moon (EDP)
also.notes: Cool, silvery iris over earthy angelica seed, cedar bark and vetiver with a green snap of galbanum.

also.name: Castaña (EDP)
also.notes: Roasted street chestnuts with a trace of caramel, then vetiver, cardamom and red pepper softened by jasmine.

also.name: Énbarr (EDP)
also.notes: A mythical horse in perfume: geranium and saffron over polished oud and saddle leather.

name: The Burren Perfumery
about: A small perfumery in the limestone Burren region of County Clare, run by perfumer Sadie Chowen. Scents are blended and bottled by hand and built around the area's wildflowers, mosses, ferns and woods, alongside organic soaps and lotions.
why: The most 'Irish landscape' perfumes you can buy, and a place you can visit. If you can't get there, the nine-scent sample library is an affordable way to smell everything.

sig.name: Ilaun (Eau de Parfum)
sig.profile: A light summer's-day scent: a wild orchid that grows in the Burren, settling onto a cool green base of fern, lichen and moss. Fresh and gentle rather than sweet.

price.note: The shop doesn't list the bottle size.

try.label: Perfume Experience Library (9 × 2 ml, every scent)

also.name: Winter Woods (EDT)
also.notes: Rosemary, bergamot and lemon, then iris and lavender, drying to cedar, pine and vetiver. Quiet and woody.

also.name: Wild Rose (EDP)
also.notes: Dawn in the Burren: pink grapefruit and bergamot, a soft centifolia rose, then honey and sandalwood.

also.name: Autumn Harvest (EDP)
also.notes: Mint over rhubarb and blackcurrant, hazelnut and wood sage, then tonka and vetiver. Early-autumn orchard.

also.name: Aran (EDT)
also.notes: A fresh sea cologne for anyone: citrus on top, mossy, lichen-and-bark woods underneath.

name: STORIES Parfums
about: A Northern Irish perfume brand founded by Tonya Kidd-Beggs in 2018, with a small line of story-led eaux de parfum plus matching body care.
why: An easy-to-wear, giftable Irish-made pair of scents, with 15 ml travel bottles that fit in a carry-on.

sig.name: STORIES Nº.01 (Eau de Parfum)
sig.profile: Bright citrus and orange blossom over a soft, slightly powdery heart of jasmine, heliotrope and fig tea, settling into warm amber and sandalwood. Polished and versatile.

also.name: STORIES Nº.02 (EDP)
also.notes: Rose, ginger, cardamom and green tea over honeyed tobacco and cedar, with opoponax, tonka and musk.

name: Inis (Fragrances of Ireland)
about: An Irish-made fragrance line sold widely in Irish pharmacies and gift shops, best known for one sea-inspired cologne and matching body care and diffusers.
why: The affordable Irish souvenir scent: easy to find, unisex, and under €40 for a big bottle.

sig.name: Inis The Energy of the Sea (Cologne)
sig.profile: A breezy, clean cologne meant to smell like a walk on the Atlantic coast: fizzy citrus, a little warm spice and soft sandalwood. Light and unisex.

price.note: Price at an Irish pharmacy.

name: Meleg Perfumes
about: A Canadian artisan house run by perfumer Matthew Meleg, making small-batch incense perfumes with a high share of natural resins.
why: A Canadian-made way to smell the ancient Egyptian temple-incense idea (see kyphi in Traditions). The maker says it's inspired by a formula carved at the Temple of Horus in Edfu, which isn't the same as being that recipe.

sig.name: Temple of Horus
sig.profile: Bright, lemony frankincense lifted by juniper and cardamom, sinking into warm, balsamic myrrh and benzoin. Like walking into a stone temple where resin has just been lit.

also.name: Temple of Horus 2 (Myrrh & Floral Suede)
also.notes: Pink lotus and soft florals over myrrh and powdery orris butter, drying to cedar and tonka. The smoother, daytime version.

name: LVNEA
about: A Montreal botanical perfumer and apothecary. Perfumes are made by hand from essential oils, absolutes and other plant materials, and the shop also sells those raw materials to people who make their own.
why: Canadian forest in a bottle, and the easiest Canadian shop for perfume raw materials (Haitian vetiver, frankincense, ylang-ylang, rose absolute) if you want to smell the ingredients behind the traditions.

sig.name: Ghost Pine (Eau de Parfum)
sig.profile: An early-morning walk in the northern forest: sweet, resinous pine needles and cold air, then bark, old roots and wet moss. Balsamic and woody rather than air-freshener pine.

also.name: Forêt Dormante (EDP)
also.notes: A waking forest with flowers: bergamot and evergreens, cardamom and lavender, rose and neroli, then frankincense, tree sap and moss.

name: Le Falcone
about: A Dubai-made affordable perfume brand. Its Bonita line comes in round, handbag-shaped bottles with a braided handle and a hanging tag.
why: Full 100 ml bottles for around £22, and the handbag bottle is part of the bag-as-accessory trend.

sig.name: Bonita Pour Femme (Eau de Parfum)
sig.profile: A bright, dewy floral: citrus and lavender, then tropical fruit with lily and lily of the valley, settling into soft vanilla sandalwood. Easy, sweet and everyday.

price.note: UK retailer price; no brand shop price found.

also.name: Bonita Hot Pink (EDP)
also.notes: Sorbet, lily, bergamot and mandarin, then jasmine, bougainvillea and pink pepper over clean musk and an earthy base.

also.name: Bonita Coco Mango (EDP)
also.notes: The yellow bottle in the set; notes not yet checked.

name: Waters + Wild
about: A West Cork organic perfume and skincare house started in 2016 by Joan Woods and June Housden, first made in an old barn near Union Hall. It uses local materials such as seaweed absolute.
why: Billed as Ireland's first organic perfume and named a 'One to Watch' at the Pitti Fragranze fair in Florence. Small, coastal and hard to find outside Ireland.

sig.name: Rose + Oud
sig.profile: A natural rose deepened with dark, woody oud. Rich but soft, as organic perfumes tend to sit close to the skin.

price.note: 'From €45' in the Irish Times; size not stated.

also.name: Tuberose + Frankincense
also.notes: Creamy tuberose with resinous frankincense; a classic, rich pairing.

also.name: Cedarwood + Cognac
also.notes: Warm, earthy cedar with a boozy edge.

name: Cozy (Khamreya)
city: Port Said (sold at Lili's Room, Helnan Walk, Port Fouad)
about: A small Egyptian body-care brand selling khamreya, a shimmering scented body product poured into glass decanters, in a range of sweet, powdery and oud scents. Orders go through its Instagram messages, where staff help pick a scent.
why: A local Egyptian take on the khumra idea (perfumed body care from the Nile region), sold in huge bottles made for sharing.

sig.name: Khamreya (400 ml)
sig.profile: Scents include Vanilla Oud, Coconut Vanilla, Sugar Babe, Feminine Energy (a soft powdery one), Thousand Wishes and Fakhama Night (white oud). Individual notes aren't published.

price.note: From the brand's Instagram post; message the brand to order.

try.label: XL (about 1.5 kg) with 6 empty bottles to split with friends
try.note: Works out to about 130 EGP a share, per the brand.
